# OPERATIVE REPORT: LEFT UPPER EXTREMITY RECONSTRUCTION 



PATIENT	DOB	MRN	DATE OF SERVICE
Dax Vance	04/12/2001	940-2281-A	09/07/2023



## Operative Details 

Date of Surgery: 2023-09-07 
Surgeon: Dr. Myrtle Turner, MD, FACS 
Assistant: Dr. Charles Vance, MD (Resident) 
Preoperative Diagnosis: 
Open compound mid-shaft left humerus fracture 
Displaced spiral fracture of the left distal radius 
Postoperative Diagnosis: Same 
Procedure Performed: 
Thorough irrigation and debridement of 2.5cm open wound, left upper arm. 
Open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of left humerus fracture with an 8-hole dynamic compression plate and screws. 
Open reduction and internal fixation (ORIF) of left distal radius fracture with a volar locking plate and screws. 
Repair of disrupted local extensor tendon sheath, left wrist. 

## Surgical Narrative 

The patient was brought to the operating room and general endotracheal anesthesia was induced. The left upper extremity was prepped and draped in the standard sterile fashion. First, the open wound overlying the humerus mid-shaft was explored, irrigated with 3 liters of normal saline under pulse lavage, and non-viable muscle tissue was debrided. The humerus fracture fragments were identified, showing a high degree of spiral displacement. Using bone reduction forceps, the fragments were anatomic-ally aligned. An 8-hole dynamic compression plate was selected and secured across the fracture with cortical and cancellous screws. Rigid fixation was achieved. 

Attention was then turned to the left forearm. A volar incision was made over the distal radius. The spiral distal radius fracture was exposed. The bone fragments were carefully aligned. A volar locking plate was positioned and stabilized with locking screws. Fluoroscopic imaging confirmed excellent anatomic alignment and hardware placement. The extensor tendon sheath was repaired with 4-0 Vicryl. The surgical wounds were closed in layers. Sterile dressing and a sugar-tong splint were applied.

## DISCHARGE SUMMARY 

PATIENT Dax Vance 

DOB 04/12/2001 

MRN 940-2281-A 

DATE OF SERVICE 09/08/2023 

## Clinical Course 

Patient Dax Vance was admitted on 2023-09-04 following a severe MVA. Following orthopedic stabilization, the patient underwent successful left arm reconstruction on 2023-09-07. He tolerated the surgery well, and post- operative pain has been reasonably controlled on a combination of oral Oxycodone and Ibuprofen. Wound sites are clean, dry, and intact with no signs of infection. The distal neurovascular status of the left arm is improved, with radial pulses at 2+ and capillary refill at <2 seconds. Sensory deficit over radial nerve distribution is slowly resolving but remains slightly diminished. Patient's neck and back pain remain moderate, which are treated conservatively with muscle relaxants and soft collar as needed. 

## Discharge Instructions 

Activity: Strictly non-weight bearing on the left arm. Keep splint dry. No heavy lifting. 
Pain Control: Oxycodone 5mg (1-2 tablets every 6 hours PRN) for 14 days, then transition to Ibuprofen. 
Referrals: Follow up with Dr. Myrtle Turner in 2 weeks for staple removal. Prescribed physical therapy 3 times per week for 6 months once surgical incisions are fully healed, focusing on left shoulder, arm, wrist, and cervical spine mobilization. 
Warn of signs of infection or deep vein thrombosis (DVT).
